problem: Prior VLN planners rely on implicit feature aggregation or on external, standalone perception/prediction modules (scene graphs, view-based future prediction). The former lacks explicit scene understanding; the latter suffers information loss and cascading errors, and view-based prediction forces the planner to reconcile fragmented panorama-face embeddings.
motivation: Objects act as landmarks in instructions and their spatial relations constrain grounding, so explicit perception and forward-looking prediction should help alignment. End-to-end perception-prediction-planning pipelines in autonomous driving (UniAD, ST-P3) reduce error accumulation, which motivates transferring the idea to VLN with a unified BEV representation.
key_idea: Unify object-level and map-level perception, waypoint and map-based future-scene prediction, and planning in one differentiable BEV-based network, passing intermediate features (not decoded symbols) to the planner.
insight: Every intermediate module contributes: removing any decoder lowers SR (e.g. R2R-CE SR 62.17 full vs 61.22 w/o scene decoder, REVERIE SR 55.98 vs 50.96 base). The end-to-end design beats independently trained modular design on all benchmarks (REVERIE SR 55.98 vs 54.15). Map-semantics targets taken from the VLM last-token latent work best (V_i vs template text or visual encodings), and a 15x15 BEV (0.5m cells) is the best trade-off.
method: BEV encoder: LSS lifts panoramic multi-view features into 3D and projects to a BEV tensor, refined by an L_b-layer deformable self-attention encoder.

Object-level perception: N_o learnable queries with a deformable cross-attention decoder over BEV, with classification and box heads supervised by Matterport3D annotations (BEVFormer-style loss); the object features O feed the planner.

Map-level perception: learnable H×W query decoded against BEV gives map features M, downsampled to a latent code m regressed (MSE) to the last-token hidden state of a VLM given the top-down semantic map plus a template description.

Waypoint-level prediction: multi-attention decoder (self-attn plus parallel cross-attn to B, O, M, fused linearly) yields a heatmap via transposed convs; NMS and depth filtering give candidate waypoints (simulator waypoints in discrete envs).
Scene-level prediction: waypoint-conditioned deformable cross-attention over M regresses future map-semantic features per waypoint (MSE); this builds a local future graph G_f.

Planning: three scores—immediate scene grounding (BEV query attends O, M, W then instruction), prospective future evaluation (graph transformer on G_f), global memory correction (global graph, BEVSceneGraph-style)—fused hierarchically by learnable sigmoid-weighted layers; argmax picks the waypoint.

Training: 200k-iteration pretraining (MLM, SAP, OG for REVERIE, plus perception/prediction losses; perception-only for first 5k), then 50k-iteration fine-tuning with teacher/student forcing, backbone and intermediate modules frozen, only planner updated.

setting.backbone: LSS + deformable-attention BEV transformer with object, map, waypoint, scene decoders and a graph-transformer planner (trained from scratch; VLM used only to generate map-semantic GT)
setting.training_data: REVERIE / R2R-CE / RxR-CE (and R2R/RxR) training data with Matterport3D object and semantic annotations; VLM-derived map-semantic labels; pretraining with MLM, SAP, OG
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph candidates (REVERIE, R2R, RxR); predicted waypoints in continuous Habitat (R2R-CE, RxR-CE)
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (REVERIE, R2R, RxR); Habitat (R2R-CE, RxR-CE)
setting.privileged: Matterport3D object and semantic annotations used as training supervision only; simulator-provided waypoints in discrete environments; none at test time otherwise

results: P3Nav sets SOTA on REVERIE test-unseen (SR 60.06, RGS 39.75 vs GOAT 57.72/38.32), R2R-CE (SR 62, SPL 52, NE 4.39 vs G3D-LF 61/52/4.53) and RxR-CE (SR 58.01, SDTW 48.04 vs G3D-LF 57.10/47.61). On REVERIE val-unseen SR ties VER at 55.98, but SPL is lower than VER (36.78 vs 39.66). Gains over BEVBert are +4.16 SPL and +4.47 RGSPL on REVERIE test.
limitations: Gains over the strongest baselines are small (about 1 point) and no variance or seeds are reported.
Needs Matterport3D object/semantic annotations and a VLM to build training targets, and adds many modules; compute and latency are not analysed.
REVERIE SPL/RGSPL do not beat VER/GOAT on val-unseen; real-world evidence is qualitative only.
